Common names: alkyl group + “alcohol” (CH3OH, methyl alcohol); the simplest hydroxy derivative of benzene is phenol, and its disubstituted derivatives are named ortho (1,2), meta (1,3) and para (1,4). Consider the following chemical reaction and identify the intermediate involved in the reaction.
  1. o-OHC–C6H4–O−Na+ (sodium salicylaldehyde phenoxide)
  2. o-Cl2HC–C6H4–O−Na+ (dichloromethyl phenoxide)

Q762CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q16NTA final key

Q763CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q17NTA final key

Q767CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived

Q769CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived

Q771CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived

  1. Only −CHO
  2. Only −COOH
  3. Both −OH and −CHO
  4. Both −OH and −COOH
Concept to recallKolbe: phenol → salicylic acid. Reimer–Tiemann puts –CHO on a phenol ring and keeps the –OH.
  1. A = salicylic acid; B = the acid chloride.
  2. The question intends C = o-cresol (the side chain reduced to CH3, the phenolic –OH untouched).
  3. Reimer–Tiemann on o-cresol gives a hydroxy-methylbenzaldehyde: D has –OH and –CHO.

Answer: option (3) — Both −OH and −CHO

TrapReimer–Tiemann gives an aldehyde, not an acid (that is Kolbe).
NoteThe middle step is loose chemistry: Clemmensen reduction works on aldehydes and ketones, not on an acid chloride. The last step settles the answer anyway, since Reimer–Tiemann always leaves both –OH and –CHO.

What happens when C6H5-O-R is treated with HX?

Q786CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q46NTA final key
Passage (summarised): ethers

Ethers are formed when a hydrogen of a hydrocarbon is replaced by an alkoxy or aryloxy group (the paper prints “carboxyl”); they are symmetrical or unsymmetrical according to the two groups on oxygen. Diethyl ether was long used as an inhalation anaesthetic. Ethers are made by acid-catalysed intermolecular dehydration of alcohols, which is not generally preferred because it gives a mixture of elimination and substitution products, and by Williamson’s synthesis, in which an alkyl halide reacts with a sodium alkoxide; ethers with substituted alkyl groups can also be made this way. The C–O bond is weakly polar and is cleaved only under drastic conditions by excess hydrogen halide. In electrophilic substitution the alkoxy group directs the incoming group to the ortho and para positions (the paper says it “deactivates” the ring: in fact it activates it).

When ethanol is dehydrated in the presence of H2SO4 at 443K and 413 K respectively the products formed are
  1. Ethane and ethoxythane
  2. Ethylmethyl ether and butene
  3. Ethylmethyl ether and propene
  4. Ethene and ethoxyethane
Concept to recallEthanol + conc. H2SO4: 443 K → ethene (intramolecular elimination); 413 K → ethoxyethane (intermolecular dehydration, SN2).
  1. At 443 K: CH3CH2OH → CH2=CH2 + H2O.
  2. At 413 K: 2CH3CH2OH → C2H5OC2H5 + H2O.
  3. The products, in the order asked, are ethene and ethoxyethane.

Answer: option (4) — Ethene and ethoxyethane

Trap“Ethane” (option 1) is an alkane: dehydration gives the alkene, ethene.

The major product in the reaction of anisole with bromine in ethanoic acid, is:

  2. p- bromoanisole

Concept to recall–OCH3 is an activating o/p director. Bromination of anisole in ethanoic acid (no Lewis acid needed) gives mainly the para isomer, the ortho isomer being minor because of steric hindrance.
  1. OCH3 releases electrons into the ring by resonance: o/p attack.

Q788CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q48NTA final key
Passage (summarised): ethers

Ethers are formed when a hydrogen of a hydrocarbon is replaced by an alkoxy or aryloxy group (the paper prints “carboxyl”); they are symmetrical or unsymmetrical according to the two groups on oxygen. Diethyl ether was long used as an inhalation anaesthetic. Ethers are made by acid-catalysed intermolecular dehydration of alcohols, which is not generally preferred because it gives a mixture of elimination and substitution products, and by Williamson’s synthesis, in which an alkyl halide reacts with a sodium alkoxide; ethers with substituted alkyl groups can also be made this way. The C–O bond is weakly polar and is cleaved only under drastic conditions by excess hydrogen halide. In electrophilic substitution the alkoxy group directs the incoming group to the ortho and para positions (the paper says it “deactivates” the ring: in fact it activates it).

In Williamson synthesis, the alkoxide ion attacks the alkyl halide via which pathway?
  1. SN2
  2. SN1
  3. Depends on nature of alkoxide ion
  4. Depends on the nature of Alkyl halide
Concept to recallWilliamson: R–X + R′–O−Na+ → R–O–R′ + NaX by SN2; best with primary halides (tertiary halides eliminate instead).
  1. The alkoxide is a strong nucleophile and attacks the halide-bearing carbon from the back.
  2. One concerted step: SN2.

Answer: option (1) — SN2

NoteThe paper prints the options as SN2 and SN1.

  2. HCl
  3. HBr

Answer: option (4) — HI

Q809CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q10 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Identify the correct structure of the compounds whose IUPAC names are respectively as follows:
(i) 4-Chloro-3-ethylbutan-1-ol and (ii) Cyclopent-3-en-1-ol
  1. (i) ClCH2–CH(C2H5)–CH2–CH2OH; (ii) as drawn for option 1
  2. (i) C2H5–CH(Cl)–CH2CH2CH2OH; (ii) as drawn for option 2
  3. (i) C2H5CH2–CH(Cl)–CH2–CH(OH)–CH3; (ii) as drawn for option 3
  4. (i) HO–CH(Cl)–CH(C2H5)–CH2CH3; (ii) as drawn for option 4

  2. Pentanal, n-Butane, Ethoxyethane, Pentan-1-ol
  3. n-Butane, Pentanal, Ethoxyethane, Pentan-1-ol
  4. n-Butane, Ethoxyethane, Pentanal, Pentan-1-ol
Concept to recallBoiling point rises with intermolecular force: London (alkane) < weak dipole (ether) < strong dipole (aldehyde) < H-bonding (alcohol); also rises with molar mass.

Q815CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q20NTA final key
In the reaction, (CH3)3C – O – CH3 + HI → Products
CH3OH and (CH3)3CI are the products and not CH3I and (CH3)3C – OH. It is because,
  1. (A) in step 2 of the reaction the departure of leaving group (HO – CH3) creates less stable carbocation.
  2. (B) in step 2 of the reaction the departure of leaving group (HO – CH3) creates more stable carbocation.
  3. (C) the reaction follows SN1 mechanism.
  4. (D) the reaction follows SN2 mechanism.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (B) and (D) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (A) and (D) only
  4. (A) and (C) only
Concept to recallWith a tertiary alkyl group the protonated ether cleaves by SN1: the C–O bond to the tertiary carbon breaks to give the stable 3° carbocation, which I− then captures.
  1. Step 1: protonation of the ether oxygen.
  2. Step 2: CH3OH leaves, generating (CH3)3C+, a stable tertiary carbocation (B).
  3. Step 3: I− attacks the carbocation (SN1, C) giving (CH3)3CI.

Answer: option (2) — (B) and (C) only

TrapWith two primary/methyl groups (e.g. CH3OC2H5) the mechanism is SN2 and I− attacks the smaller group.
Q816CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q28NTA final key
In the following table, match the reactants given in List-I with the correct product in List-II as per the reaction of hydration of alkene under acidic condition.
List-I (Reactants)List-II (Products)
(A) 3-methylhex-2-ene, CH3CH2CH2C(CH3)=CHCH3(I) 1-methylcyclohexan-1-ol
(B) 1-methylcyclohexene(II) 3-methylhexan-3-ol
(C) but-2-ene, CH3CH=CHCH3(III) 2-cyclohexylbutan-2-ol
(D) 2-cyclohexylidenebutane, (CH2)5C=C(CH3)CH2CH3(IV) butan-2-ol
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)
  3. (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallAcid-catalysed hydration follows Markovnikov’s rule through the more stable carbocation: OH ends up on the more substituted carbon of the C=C.
  1. A: H+ adds to the =CH, giving the tertiary cation at C-3 → 3-methylhexan-3-ol (II).
  2. B: tertiary cation at the methyl-bearing ring carbon → 1-methylcyclohexan-1-ol (I).
  3. C: symmetrical → butan-2-ol (IV).
  4. D: both alkene carbons are fully substituted, so either could carry the OH; OH on the open-chain carbon (bearing CH3 and C2H5) gives 2-cyclohexylbutan-2-ol, the only matching product (III). Matching A, B, C first leaves III anyway.
  5. A–II, B–I, C–IV, D–III.

Answer: option (3) — (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)

NoteThe paper draws all eight structures as skeletal formulae; they are named here.

  3. (B) < (A) < (D) < (C)
  4. (C) < (B) < (D) < (A)
Concept to recallLower pH = stronger acid. −NO2 (−I, −R) stabilises phenoxide, most strongly from o/p (resonance); −CH3 (+I) destabilises it.

  2. Increasing pH is the same sequence: (A) < (C) < (D) < (B).

Q821CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q24NTA final key
Which among the following compounds is most soluble in water ?
  1. Ethanol
  2. Ethane
  3. Phenol
  4. Ethylene glycol
Concept to recallSolubility in water rises with the number of −OH groups that can H-bond with water, and falls with the size of the hydrocarbon part.
  1. Ethane: non-polar, insoluble. Phenol: sparingly soluble (large aryl group).
  2. Ethanol: one −OH; ethylene glycol: two −OH on a C2 skeleton → most H-bonding.
  3. Ethylene glycol is the most soluble.

Answer: option (4) — Ethylene glycol

  2. Phenol
  3. Propanone
  4. Propene
Concept to recallCumene process: cumene + O2 → cumene hydroperoxide →(H+, H2O) phenol + acetone.
  1. Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised in air to its hydroperoxide.
  2. Acid hydrolysis gives phenol (and acetone as by-product).
  3. The cumene process is the commercial route to phenol.

Answer: option (2) — Phenol

NotePropanone is also formed, but NCERT presents the cumene process as the preparation of phenol, with acetone as a by-product; NTA keys phenol.

  1. SN1
  2. SN2

Q831CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q24NTA final key
The following is not an appropriate reaction for preparation of t-butyl ethyl ether because :
C2H5ONa + (CH3)3C–Cl → (CH3)3C–OC2H5
  1. Sodium ethoxide is a weak base
  2. Alkyl halide is tertiary in nature
  3. Sodium ethoxide is a strong base
  4. The ether formed is very bulky
Concept to recallWilliamson synthesis is SN2: use a 1° halide; a strong base on a 3° halide gives E2 elimination.
  1. C2H5O− is a strong base; with the crowded 3° halide it pulls off a β-H.
  2. Product is 2-methylpropene, not the ether.

Answer: option (3) — Sodium ethoxide is a strong base

Trap(2) is also a true statement about the halide; NTA keyed the base strength as “the” reason.
NoteBoth facts — the halide is tertiary and ethoxide is a strong base — together cause elimination; NTA’s final key is (3), the strong base. The right route is (CH3)3CONa + C2H5Cl.

  4. 2-Ethyl-3-bromobut-2-en-1-ol

  2. Substituents: Br on C2, CH3 on C3; double bond at 2.
  3. 2-Bromo-3-methylpent-2-en-1-ol.

Q850CUET 2023 · 08 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q15key re-derived
Identify the stereochemically correct product(s) formed from the following:

Concept to recallAn ester + 2 RMgX gives a 3° alcohol from the acyl part and an alkoxide from the OR part. The O–C(alkyl) bond is never broken, so the stereocentre keeps its configuration.

TrapSwapping the wedge and hash of two groups (options 2 and 4) inverts the centre; no bond to it breaks, so inversion is impossible.

Q859CUET 2023 · 13 Jun, Shift 3 · Q15 · Prepp reconstructionworked here
CH3–C(CH3)(Ph)–CH=CH2 →(H3O+) ? Product formed is:
  1. CH3–C(CH3)(Ph)–CH(OH)–CH3

  3. CH3–C(OH)(Ph)–CH(CH3)–CH3
  4. CH3–C(OH)(Ph)–CH2–CH2–CH3
Concept to recallAcid-catalysed hydration: Markovnikov carbocation, which rearranges (1,2-shift) if a more stable cation can form.
  1. H+ adds to the terminal CH2: secondary cation on C-2, next to C(CH3)(Ph).
  2. A CH3 moves from C-3 to C-2 with its electron pair: the cation is now on C-3, tertiary and benzylic (most stable).
  3. Water captures it: CH3–C(OH)(Ph)–CH(CH3)2, 3-methyl-2-phenylbutan-2-ol.

Answer: option (3) — CH3–C(OH)(Ph)–CH(CH3)–CH3

TrapWriting the Markovnikov product without checking whether the carbocation can rearrange.
NotePrepp’s key prints (1), the product without rearrangement. Hydration goes through a carbocation; the secondary cation next to a quaternary carbon rearranges by a 1,2-methyl shift to the tertiary benzylic cation, giving (3). (A phenyl shift instead would give option (2), a tertiary but non-benzylic cation, so (3) is the expected major product.)

Q878CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q26NTA final key
Among the following ethers, which cannot react with HI?

  2. C6H5–OCH3 (anisole)
  3. C6H5–O–C6H5 (diphenyl ether)
  4. C6H5–O–C6H11 (cyclohexyl phenyl ether)

Q879CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q8NTA final key
During bromination of phenol, lewis acid is not necessary required because of:
  1. Electromeric effect
  2. Inductive effect of −OH group
  3. +R effect of −OH group
  4. Deactivating effect of −OH group
Concept to recall−OH donates a lone pair into the ring (+R / +M), raising electron density at o- and p-positions: the ring is strongly activated.
  1. Benzene needs FeBr3 to polarise Br2 into Br+.
  2. In phenol the +R effect of −OH makes the ring so electron-rich that Br2 itself is polarised by the ring; no Lewis acid is needed (bromine water even gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol).

Answer: option (3) — +R effect of −OH group

TrapThe −I effect of oxygen withdraws electrons; it is outweighed by +R, so (2) and (4) are wrong.
Q880CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q15NTA final key

  2. Lone pair–lone pair repulsion on O reduces it to 108.9° (NCERT).

Q881CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q23NTA final key

  4. Cyclopropanecarboxylic acid (option 4 above)

  1. A: cyclopropene (dehydration).
  2. B: 2-chlorocyclopropan-1-ol (chlorohydrin).
  3. C: 2-hydroxycyclopropane-1-carbonitrile.
  4. D: 2-hydroxycyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid.

Q883CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key

  2. B and C only

  3. C: C-2 carries OH and two carbons ⇒ secondary (C-1 OH is primary).

Q884CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q31NTA final key
Which of the following does not depict an isomer of oxetane?
  1. 2-Methyloxirane
  2. CH3–O–CH2–CO–O–CH3
  3. Cyclopropanol
  4. CH2=CH–O–CH3 (methyl vinyl ether)

Q885CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q36NTA final key
Which of the following statements relating to the acidic character of alcohols is not true?
  1. It is due to the polar nature of OH bond.
  2. Increases with an attachment of e− withdrawing group.
  3. Alcohols are weaker acids than water.
  4. Alcohols behave as electrophiles.
Concept to recallAlcohols are Brønsted acids because the O–H bond is polar; electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the alkoxide and raise acidity; alkyl groups (+I) make them weaker acids than water.
  1. (1), (2), (3) are NCERT statements about the acidity of alcohols.
  2. (4) is not a statement about acidic character: as acids alcohols donate a proton (the O–H acts with a base), they are not acting as electrophiles.

Answer: option (4) — Alcohols behave as electrophiles.

Q886CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q9NTA final key

  2. Hydrolysis of the −CHCl2 group gives −CHO: salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde).

Q887CUET 2022 · 10 Aug, Shift 1 (SET 06) · Q28NTA final key

Q888CUET 2022 · 10 Aug, Shift 1 (SET 06) · Q29NTA final key
Among the following statements, choose the correct statements.
(A) Boiling point of alcohols increases with increase in the number of carbon atoms.
(B) In alcohols, boiling points increases with increase of branching in carbon chain.
(C) Boiling points of alcohols are lesser in comparison to haloalkanes of comparable molecular mass.
(D) Boiling points of alcohols are higher in comparison to hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass.
(E) The high boiling points of alcohols are mainly due to the presence of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, D and E only
  2. A, B and C only
  3. B, C and D only
  4. C, D and E only
Concept to recallAlcohols: b.p. rises with chain length, falls with branching (smaller surface area), and is high because of intermolecular H-bonding.
  1. A true; D true.
  2. B false (branching lowers b.p.); C false (alcohols boil higher than haloalkanes).
  3. E is meant to be the H-bonding statement; with “intermolecular” it is true ⇒ A, D, E.

Answer: option (1) — A, D and E only

TrapIntramolecular H-bonding lowers b.p. (e.g. o-nitrophenol); the alcohol effect is intermolecular.
NoteNTA’s final key is (1), “A, D and E only”. As printed, statement E says intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which is wrong: the high boiling points of alcohols are due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding (NCERT). Strictly only A and D are correct, which no option offers; NTA evidently read E as “intermolecular”. NTA’s answer is kept.

Q891CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q25NTA final key

  1. sp3
  2. sp2
  3. sp2d
  4. spd2

  1. CH3CHO + HCN → CH3CH(OH)CN (ethanal cyanohydrin).
  2. The former C=O carbon now has four single bonds (CH3, H, OH, CN): sp3.

Q892CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q27NTA final key

  2. (D), (C), (A), (B)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (C), (B), (D), (A)

  1. (D) p-methoxybenzoic acid: +R donor, least acidic.
  2. (C) benzoic acid: reference.
  3. (A) one p-NO2: more acidic; (B) two NO2 (o, p): most acidic.

Q893CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q28NTA final key

  1. KMnO4
  2. LiAlH4 and ether
  3. NaOH and CaO
  4. B2H6 (Diborane)
Concept to recallDecarboxylation: the sodium salt heated with soda-lime (NaOH + CaO) loses CO2: RCOONa → R–H + Na2CO3.
  1. Soda-lime removes the COOH carbon as carbonate, leaving the alkane with one carbon fewer.
  2. LiAlH4 and B2H6 reduce RCOOH to the alcohol; KMnO4 oxidises.

Answer: option (3) — NaOH and CaO

Q894CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
Sodium benzoate finds applications in
  1. Perfumes
  2. Nylon 6,6
  3. Soaps and detergents
  4. Food preservatives
Concept to recallNCERT uses of carboxylic acids: sodium benzoate is a food preservative; higher fatty acids make soaps; adipic acid makes nylon-6,6; esters go into perfumes.
  1. Sodium benzoate (E211) is the standard food preservative.

Answer: option (4) — Food preservatives

Q895CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q30NTA final key
Iodoform reaction with sodium hypoiodite is used for detection of
  1. CH3CO group
  2. CH3CO and CH3CH(OH) groups
  3. CH3O group
  4. (CH3)3CO group
Concept to recallNaOI gives a yellow CHI3 precipitate with methyl ketones/ethanal (CH3CO–) and with alcohols CH3CH(OH)–, which NaOI first oxidises to CH3CO–.
  1. CH3CO– is halogenated to CI3CO– and cleaved to CHI3.
  2. CH3CH(OH)– is oxidised by hypoiodite to CH3CO–, so it also responds (ethanol, propan-2-ol).

Answer: option (2) — CH3CO and CH3CH(OH) groups

Q896CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q10NTA final key
The major product Z in the following chemical reaction is
C6H5CHO + C6H5COCH3 →(OH−, 293 K) Z
  1. C6H5COCH=CHC6H5
  2. C6H5COCOC6H5

  4. C6H5CH(OH)CH(OH)C6H5
Concept to recallClaisen–Schmidt (cross aldol): a ketone with α-H + an aldehyde without α-H in dilute alkali → α,β-unsaturated ketone.
  1. The enolate of acetophenone (from its CH3) attacks benzaldehyde.
  2. The β-hydroxy ketone dehydrates (conjugation with both rings) to C6H5COCH=CHC6H5, chalcone (1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one).

Q897CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q12NTA final key
The reagent used in the Stephen reaction is
  1. Pd-BaSO4 + H2
  2. SnCl2 + HCl
  3. AlH(i-Bu)2 + H2O
  4. DIBAL-H + H2O
Concept to recallStephen reaction: RCN + SnCl2/HCl → imine hydrochloride →(H3O+) RCHO.
  1. Nitriles are reduced by stannous chloride in HCl to the imine, which hydrolyses to the aldehyde.
  2. Pd–BaSO4/H2 is Rosenmund (acid chloride); DIBAL-H also converts nitriles to aldehydes but is not the Stephen reagent.

Answer: option (2) — SnCl2 + HCl

Q898CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q18NTA final key
Which of the following reaction will not result in the formation of C–C bonds?
  1. Wurtz reaction
  2. Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction
  3. Reimer-Tiemann reaction
  4. Cannizzaro reaction
Concept to recallCannizzaro: 2HCHO + conc. NaOH → CH3OH + HCOONa, a hydride transfer (redox), no new C–C bond.
  1. Wurtz joins two alkyl groups; Friedel–Crafts acylation joins acyl C to the ring; Reimer–Tiemann attaches CHO carbon to the ring.
  2. Cannizzaro only oxidises one aldehyde and reduces the other: no C–C bond.

Answer: option (4) — Cannizzaro reaction

Q899CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q19NTA final key
What is the final product X in the following reaction?
CH3–CH2–CH2–CHO →(Ammoniacal AgNO3; H3O+) X

  2. CH3CH2CH2COOH
  3. CH3CH2CH2CH2NO2
  4. CH3CH2CH2CH3
Concept to recallTollens’ reagent oxidises an aldehyde to the carboxylate (silver mirror); acidification gives the acid.
  1. RCHO + 2[Ag(NH3)2]+ + 3OH− → RCOO− + 2Ag + 2H2O + 4NH3.
  2. H3O+: butanoic acid.

Answer: option (2) — CH3CH2CH2COOH

Q900CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q30NTA final key
Which of the following compounds does not undergo Cannizzaro reaction?
  1. Formaldehyde
  2. 2,2-Dimethylbutanal
  3. Benzaldehyde
  4. Acetaldehyde
Concept to recallCannizzaro needs an aldehyde with no α-H; an aldehyde with α-H undergoes aldol condensation instead.
  1. HCHO, C6H5CHO and 2,2-dimethylbutanal (quaternary α-C) have no α-H.
  2. Acetaldehyde has three α-H, so it gives aldol, not Cannizzaro.

Answer: option (4) — Acetaldehyde

Q901CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
The IUPAC name of CH3–CH2–CHO is:
  1. Propanone
  2. Propanal
  3. Propanoic acid
  4. Ethanol
Concept to recallAldehydes: longest chain including the CHO carbon (C-1), suffix “-al”.
  1. Three carbons including the CHO carbon: prop-.
  2. Aldehyde suffix -al: propanal.

Answer: option (2) — Propanal

Q902CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
When benzaldehyde is subjected to oxidation using acidified potassium permanganate (KMnO4), what organic product is formed?
  1. Benzyl alcohol

  3. Benzene

Q903CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
Which of the following oxidizing agents is mild enough to selectively oxidize an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid without cleaving other sensitive carbon-carbon single bonds?
  1. Tollens’ reagent
  2. Concentrated H2SO4 at high temperatures
  3. Ozone followed by Zn / H2O
  4. LiAlH4 in dry ether
Concept to recallTollens’ reagent [Ag(NH3)2]+ oxidises only the –CHO group (RCHO → RCOO−, silver mirror); ketones and C–C bonds are untouched.
  1. LiAlH4 is a reductant; ozonolysis cleaves C=C; hot concentrated acid is not a selective oxidant.
  2. Tollens’ reagent is the mild, selective one.

Answer: option (1) — Tollens’ reagent

Q904CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
What are the primary reagents and catalysts required to carry out the Gattermann-Koch reaction?
  1. CO, HCl, and anhydrous AlCl3 / CuCl
  2. CHCl3 and aqueous NaOH
  3. HCN, HCl, and anhydrous AlCl3
  4. CH3Cl and anhydrous AlCl3
Concept to recallGattermann–Koch: C6H6 + CO + HCl → C6H5CHO (anhydrous AlCl3/CuCl).
  1. CO + HCl generate the formyl electrophile (HCO+) with AlCl3/CuCl.
  2. It formylates benzene to benzaldehyde.

Q905CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Which of the following carbonyl compounds will undergo a self-oxidation and self-reduction reaction (Cannizzaro Reaction) when treated with a concentrated solution of a strong base (NaOH)?
  1. Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO)
  2. Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
  3. Acetone (CH3COCH3)
  4. Propanal (CH3CH2CHO)
Concept to recallCannizzaro: aldehydes with no α-H, with concentrated alkali, give alcohol + carboxylate salt.
  1. Acetaldehyde, propanal and acetone have α-hydrogens: they undergo aldol instead.
  2. 2C6H5CHO + NaOH → C6H5CH2OH + C6H5COONa.

Answer: option (2) — Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)

TrapAcetone is a ketone; Cannizzaro is an aldehyde reaction.
Q906CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Aldehydes and ketones react with semicarbazide (NH2NHCONH2) in a weakly acidic medium to form crystalline semicarbazone derivatives. Which of the three nitrogen atoms in a semicarbazide molecule acts as the primary nucleophilic center during this reaction?
  1. The nitrogen atom attached directly to the carbonyl carbon atom (−NH−C=O).
  2. The amide nitrogen atom of the terminal primary amide group (−CONH2).
  3. The terminal hydrazine nitrogen atom linked to the adjacent secondary nitrogen (−NH2 of the −NH−NH2 group).
  4. All three nitrogen atoms are equally nucleophilic due to resonance stabilization.
Concept to recallLone pairs on N attached to C=O are delocalised (amide resonance) and are poor nucleophiles.
  1. Both N atoms bonded to the C=O share their lone pairs with it.
  2. The terminal NH2 of the hydrazine end is not conjugated: it attacks, giving R2C=N–NHCONH2.

Answer: option (3) — The terminal hydrazine nitrogen atom linked to the adjacent secondary nitrogen (−NH2 of the −NH−NH2 group).

TrapThe “amide” NH2 looks like an amine but is deactivated by resonance.
Q907CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
Benzene reacts with a mixture of carbon monoxide (CO) and hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas in the presence of an anhydrous aluminium chloride (AlCl3) catalyst to yield Benzaldehyde. This organic transformation is officially known as the:
  1. Rosenmund Reduction
  2. Gattermann-Koch Reaction
  3. Etard Reaction
  4. Stephen Reaction
Concept to recallGattermann–Koch: ArH + CO + HCl (AlCl3/CuCl) → ArCHO.

  2. CO + HCl on benzene is Gattermann–Koch.

TrapEtard also makes benzaldehyde, but from toluene.
Q908CUET 2026 · 26 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5worked here
An organic compound P of molecular formula C6H12O3 gives positive iodoform test but negative Tollens’ test. When P is treated with dilute acid, it produces Q. Q gives positive Tollens’ test and also iodoform test. Identify compound P.
  1. CH3COCH(OCH3)CH2OCH3
  2. CH3COCH2CH(OCH3)2
  3. HCOCH2CH2CH(OCH3)2
  4. CH3COC(OCH3)2CH3
Concept to recallAn acetal R–CH(OR′)2 is a masked aldehyde: no Tollens’ test until dilute acid hydrolyses it to R–CHO. A CH3CO– group gives the iodoform test.
  1. P must have CH3CO– (iodoform +) and no free CHO (Tollens −).
  2. Q must have a free CHO after hydrolysis, so P contains an acetal CH(OCH3)2.
  3. CH3COCH2CH(OCH3)2 (C6H12O3) → CH3COCH2CHO: Tollens + and iodoform +.

Answer: option (2) — CH3COCH2CH(OCH3)2

Trap(4) gives the iodoform test both times but never an aldehyde.
NoteThe site prints (4). That compound is a ketal: hydrolysis gives CH3COCOCH3 (butanedione), which has no aldehyde group, so Q could not give the Tollens’ test. (3) has a free CHO, so P itself would be Tollens-positive. Only (2) fits every clue.
Q909CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
Which of the following reagents converts aldehydes into primary alcohols?
  1. PCC
  2. LiAlH4
  3. KMnO4

  2. LiAlH4 delivers H− to C=O: 1° alcohol.

Q910CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2worked here
An equimolar mixture of benzaldehyde and acetaldehyde is treated with dilute NaOH. The major product formed is isolated and then subjected to I2/NaOH. The number of moles of yellow precipitate obtained per mole of benzaldehyde initially taken is:

  2. 0.5
  3. 1
  4. 2
Concept to recallCross aldol (Claisen–Schmidt): C6H5CHO + CH3CHO → C6H5CH=CHCHO (cinnamaldehyde). Iodoform needs CH3CO– or CH3CH(OH)–.

  2. It has no CH3CO– or CH3CH(OH)– group: no CHI3.
  3. Moles of yellow precipitate = 0.

Q911CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
An organic compound gives a positive semicarbazide test and on reduction produces propan-2-ol. The compound is:
  1. Propanal
  2. Propanone
  3. Ethanal
  4. Methanal
Concept to recallSemicarbazone formation = a C=O group. Reduction: aldehyde → 1° alcohol, ketone → 2° alcohol.

Answer: option (2) — Propanone

Q912CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
Consider the following reaction sequence:The major product Y formed in the above reaction is:
  1. Ethanol
  2. Butanal
  3. Crotonaldehyde

Q913CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
Which reagent is used to distinguish between ethanal and propanone?
  1. Tollen’s reagent
  2. Sodium hydroxide

Q914CUET 2026 · 31 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Aldehyde A undergoes Cannizzaro reaction to give compounds B and C. Compound B on oxidation gives benzoic acid. Compound C gives positive iodoform test after suitable oxidation. Compound A is:
  1. Benzaldehyde
  2. Formaldehyde
  3. Acetaldehyde
  4. Propanal
Concept to recallOnly aldehydes without α-H (HCHO, C6H5CHO) undergo Cannizzaro.

Q915CUET 2026 · labelled 5 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain; no answers printed) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10worked here
The correct order of acidic strength is:
  1. CH3COOH > ClCH2COOH > Cl2CHCOOH > Cl3CCOOH
  2. ClCH2COOH > CH3COOH > Cl2CHCOOH > Cl3CCOOH
  3. Cl3CCOOH > Cl2CHCOOH > ClCH2COOH > CH3COOH
  4. Cl2CHCOOH > Cl3CCOOH > ClCH2COOH > CH3COOH
Concept to recallEach –Cl (−I) stabilises the carboxylate: more Cl, stronger acid.

Q916CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q27NTA final key
Hell-Volhard Zelinsky reaction is used for the formation of
  1. alcohols
  2. aldehydes
  3. ketones
  4. α-halocarboxylic acids
Concept to recallHVZ: R–CH2–COOH + X2/red P, then H2O → R–CHX–COOH (acids with α-H are halogenated at the α-carbon).
  1. Red phosphorus and Cl2 or Br2 convert the acid to an acyl halide, which enolises.
  2. The α-carbon is halogenated; hydrolysis returns the α-halo acid.

Answer: option (4) — α-halocarboxylic acids

Q917CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q28NTA final key
What is the correct sequence of increasing reactivity of the following compounds towards nucleophilic addition reaction?
  1. (A) Ethanal
  2. (B) Propanone
  3. (C) Propanal
  4. (D) Butanone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  2. (D), (B), (C), (A)
  3. (A), (C), (B), (D)
  4. (C), (B), (D), (A)
Concept to recallNucleophilic addition is slowed by alkyl groups on the carbonyl carbon (electronic: +I lowers its δ+; steric: crowding). Aldehydes > ketones; smaller > larger.
  1. Ketones are below aldehydes: butanone (ethyl + methyl) < propanone (two methyls).
  2. Among aldehydes, propanal (ethyl) < ethanal (methyl).
  3. Increasing order: butanone < propanone < propanal < ethanal = (D), (B), (C), (A).

Answer: option (2) — (D), (B), (C), (A)

Q918CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q29NTA final key
Which of the following reagent(s) is required for the conversion of Benzene to methyl benzoate?
  1. (A) Br2/FeBr3
  2. (B) Mg, dry Ether
  3. (C) CO2, H3O+
  4. (D) Methanol, Conc. H2SO4
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (C) only
  2. (A), (B) and (D) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallGrignard carboxylation: RMgX + CO2, then H3O+ → RCOOH. Fischer esterification: RCOOH + R′OH (conc. H2SO4) → RCOOR′.
  1. Benzene + Br2/FeBr3 → bromobenzene.
  2. Mg, dry ether → C6H5MgBr.
  3. CO2 then H3O+ → benzoic acid.
  4. CH3OH, conc. H2SO4 → methyl benzoate. All four steps are needed.

Answer: option (3) — (A), (B), (C) and (D)

Q919CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q30NTA final key
Which reagent will distinguish Benzophenone from acetone ?
  1. Fehling’s reagent
  2. Tollen’s reagent
  3. 2,4-DNP reagent
  4. I2/NaOH
Concept to recallIodoform test: positive for CH3CO– (methyl ketones, ethanal) and CH3CH(OH)–.
  1. Both are ketones: both give 2,4-DNP derivatives; neither reduces Fehling’s or Tollens’ reagent.
  2. Acetone, CH3COCH3, is a methyl ketone: yellow CHI3 with I2/NaOH.
  3. Benzophenone, C6H5COC6H5, has no CH3CO group: no iodoform.

Answer: option (4) — I2/NaOH

Trap2,4-DNP detects the C=O group, which both compounds have.
Q920CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 1 · Q31NTA final key
The structural feature in carbonyl compound for Aldol condensation
  1. presence of at least one β-hydrogen
  2. presence of at least one α-hydrogen
  3. Concentrated base
  4. lack of α hydrogen
Concept to recallAldol: dilute base removes an α-H to give an enolate, which adds to a second C=O. No α-H + concentrated base = Cannizzaro.
  1. The enolate can form only if the carbonyl compound has an α-hydrogen.
  2. So the structural requirement is at least one α-H (with dilute alkali).

Answer: option (2) — presence of at least one α-hydrogen

Trap“Concentrated base” and “lack of α-hydrogen” are the conditions for Cannizzaro.
Q921CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · Q13 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The reduction of cyclohexanone with LiAlH4 will give:
  1. Cyclohexanol
  2. Cyclohexanaldehyde

  2. Cyclohexanone → cyclohexanol (a 2° alcohol).

Q922CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · Q15 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Acetaldehyde on treatment with Fehling’s solution gives a precipitate of
  1. Cu2O
  2. Cu
  3. CuO
  4. Cu2O2

  2. A red-brown precipitate of cuprous oxide, Cu2O, forms.

Q923CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · Q19 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The correct order of increasing acidic strength is
  1. (A) Ethanol
  2. (B) Phenol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

  4. (B), (C), (A), (D)

Q924CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · Q9 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following compounds will respond to iodoform test?

Q925CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · Q15 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following compound will form a cyclic product on reaction with ethylene glycol?
  1. Acetone
  2. Ethylether

Q926CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · Q23 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following reactions are involved in preparation of aldehydes?
  1. (A) Gatterman-Koch reaction

Q927CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · Q26 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following compound will undergo Cannizzaro reaction?
  1. Methanal
  2. Cyclohexanone
  3. Propanal
  4. Acetone

Q941CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q41 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Passage (27 May, Q41–45): carboxylic acids

Carboxylic acids contain –COOH; higher members (fatty acids) occur in fats as glycerol esters. They are prepared by oxidising alcohols and aldehydes, by hydrolysing nitriles and amides, and from Grignard reagents. They are stronger acids than phenols and alcohols but weaker than mineral acids, and substituents change their acidity. Their reactions break the O–H or the C–OH bond; acids with an α-hydrogen are α-halogenated with halogen and red phosphorus (Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction), and aromatic acids undergo electrophilic substitution. Uses: methanoic acid in rubber, textile, dyeing, leather and electroplating; higher fatty acids for soaps and detergents; benzoate esters in perfumery.

The reagents needed for the preparation of Benzoic acid from ethyl benzene is:
  1. AgNO3/H2SO4
  2. KMnO4-KOH, H3O+
  3. H2/PtO2
  4. LiAlH4/Ether
Concept to recallAlkaline KMnO4 oxidises the whole side chain of an alkylbenzene (with a benzylic H) to –COOH, whatever its length; acidification frees benzoic acid.
  1. C6H5CH2CH3 → (KMnO4/KOH, heat) C6H5COOK → (H3O+) C6H5COOH.

Answer: option (2) — KMnO4-KOH, H3O+

Q950CUET 2024 · 15 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q17NTA final key

  2. (B) ClCH2COOH
  3. (C) FCH2COOH
  4. (D) HCOOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (D) < (A) < (B) < (C)
  2. (A) < (D) < (C) < (B)
  3. (B) < (A) < (D) < (C)
  4. (C) < (B) < (D) < (A)
Concept to recall−I effect of halogen: F > Cl > Br, so FCH2COOH is the strongest; HCOOH (no halogen) is the weakest of these. pKa: HCOOH 3.75, BrCH2COOH 2.90, ClCH2COOH 2.86, FCH2COOH 2.59.
  1. Increasing acidity = decreasing pKa: D < A < B < C.

Answer: option (1) — (D) < (A) < (B) < (C)

Q956CUET 2024 · 29 May (pen & paper, 306 E New) · Book A · Q11NTA final key
What is the colour of copper compound formed in Fehling's test for aliphatic aldehydes ?
  1. Green
  2. Blue
  3. Yellow
  4. Red brown
Concept to recallFehling’s solution (Cu2+ tartrate complex, deep blue) is reduced by aliphatic aldehydes to a red-brown precipitate of Cu2O.
  1. RCHO + 2Cu2+ + 5OH− → RCOO− + Cu2O↓ + 3H2O.
  2. Cu2O is red-brown.

Answer: option (4) — Red brown

TrapBlue is the colour of the reagent before reaction. Aromatic aldehydes do not respond.
Q957CUET 2024 · 29 May (pen & paper, 306 E New) · Book A · Q24NTA final key
Which of the following compounds will undergo Aldol condensation reaction ?
  1. (A) (structure A above)
  2. (B) (structure B above)
  3. (C) CH3-CH2-C(CH3)2-CH2-CHO
  4. (D) HCHO
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (C) and (D) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (B), (C) and (D) only
  4. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
Concept to recallAldol condensation needs at least one α-hydrogen (on the carbon next to C=O).
  1. (A): the CHO is on a carbon carrying two CH3 groups and the ring — no α-H.
  2. (B): CHO–CH2–(ring): two α-H, so it reacts.
  3. (C): CHO–CH2–C(CH3)2–…: the CH2 is α, so it reacts.
  4. (D) HCHO has no α-carbon at all: it gives the Cannizzaro reaction instead.
  5. Answer: (B) and (C) only.

Answer: option (2) — (B) and (C) only

TrapIn (C) the quaternary carbon is β, not α — look only at the carbon next to CHO.
Q958CUET 2024 · 29 May (pen & paper, 306 E New) · Book A · Q25NTA final key
Consider the following compounds :
Arrange these compounds in the increasing order of rate of hydrolysis :
  1. (B) < (D) < (C) < (A)
  2. (B) < (D) < (A) < (C)
  3. (D) < (B) < (A) < (C)
  4. (A) < (D) < (B) < (C)
Concept to recallHydrolysis of an acyl chloride is nucleophilic attack at the C=O carbon: electron-withdrawing groups (raise δ+) speed it up, electron-donating groups slow it down.
  1. −OH (+R, para) donates electrons: slowest (B).
  2. −H: reference (D).
  3. −CHO (−R, −I) withdraws: faster (A); −NO2 withdraws most: fastest (C).
  4. Increasing rate: (B) < (D) < (A) < (C).

Answer: option (2) — (B) < (D) < (A) < (C)

Q959CUET 2024 · 29 May (pen & paper, 306 E New) · Book A · Q34NTA final key
Passage (29 May 2024, Q34–38): reactivity of aldehydes and ketones

Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition, for two reasons. Steric: a ketone carries two large groups on the carbonyl carbon, which hinder the approach of the nucleophile more than the one group (and an H) of an aldehyde. Electronic: two electron-releasing alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more than one does.

(NCERT text set as printed; Q35 on amines does not draw on it.)

Which among the following compound is formed, when aldehyde reacts with HCN in presence of base ?
  1. Cyanide
  2. Isocyanide
  3. Cyanohydrin
  4. Hydrogen cyanide
Concept to recallBase generates CN−, which adds to the C=O carbon; protonation gives a cyanohydrin R–CH(OH)–CN.
  1. RCHO + HCN →(OH−) RCH(OH)CN.
  2. A carbon bearing both −OH and −CN is a cyanohydrin.

Answer: option (3) — Cyanohydrin

Q960CUET 2024 · 29 May (pen & paper, 306 E New) · Book A · Q36NTA final key
Passage (29 May 2024, Q34–38): reactivity of aldehydes and ketones

Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition, for two reasons. Steric: a ketone carries two large groups on the carbonyl carbon, which hinder the approach of the nucleophile more than the one group (and an H) of an aldehyde. Electronic: two electron-releasing alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more than one does.

(NCERT text set as printed; Q35 on amines does not draw on it.)

A new C-C bond formation is possible in :
  1. (A) Cannizzaro reaction
  2. (B) Friedel-Crafts alkylation
  3. (C) Clemmensen reduction
  4. (D) Riemer-Tiemann reaction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (D) only
  3. (B), (C) and (D) only
  4. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
Concept to recallLook for a step that joins two carbon fragments.
  1. (A) Cannizzaro: hydride transfer; products HCOO−/CH3OH — no new C–C.
  2. (B) Friedel–Crafts alkylation: Ar–R bond formed — yes.
  3. (C) Clemmensen: C=O → CH2 — no new C–C.
  4. (D) Reimer–Tiemann: :CCl2 attacks the ring → Ar–CHO — yes.
  5. Answer: (B) and (D) only.

Answer: option (1) — (B) and (D) only

Q961CUET 2024 · 29 May (pen & paper, 306 E New) · Book A · Q37NTA final key
Passage (29 May 2024, Q34–38): reactivity of aldehydes and ketones

Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition, for two reasons. Steric: a ketone carries two large groups on the carbonyl carbon, which hinder the approach of the nucleophile more than the one group (and an H) of an aldehyde. Electronic: two electron-releasing alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more than one does.

(NCERT text set as printed; Q35 on amines does not draw on it.)

Which of the following will respond to Tollen's test ?
  1. Ethanoic acid
  2. Methanoic acid
  3. Propanoic acid
  4. Butanoic acid
Concept to recallMethanoic (formic) acid H–COOH contains an aldehyde-like H–C=O and is a reducing agent.
  1. HCOOH + 2[Ag(NH3)2]+ → silver mirror (oxidised to CO2).
  2. Other carboxylic acids do not reduce Tollens’ reagent.

Answer: option (2) — Methanoic acid

Q962CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q26NTA final key
Which of the following reaction is shown by aldehydes that do not have alpha H-atom?
  1. Aldol condensation
  2. Cross aldol condensation
  3. Cannizzaro reaction
  4. Kolbe's reaction
Concept to recallNo α-H → Cannizzaro (self oxidation–reduction in conc. alkali): 2HCHO → HCOO− + CH3OH.
  1. Aldol (and cross aldol between two such aldehydes) needs an α-H to form the enolate.
  2. Aldehydes without α-H (HCHO, C6H5CHO) give the Cannizzaro reaction.

Answer: option (3) — Cannizzaro reaction

Q963CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q36NTA final key
Which of the following gives positive Tollens test ?

  2. (B) Acetophenone
  3. (C) Formic acid
  4. (D) Benzene carbaldehyde
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (A), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallTollens’ reagent oxidises all aldehydes (aliphatic and aromatic) and formic acid; ketones do not respond.
  1. (A) C6H5CH2CHO: aldehyde — yes. (D) C6H5CHO: aldehyde — yes.
  2. (C) HCOOH has an H–C=O unit — yes.
  3. (B) acetophenone C6H5COCH3 is a ketone — no.
  4. Answer: (A), (C) and (D) only.

Answer: option (4) — (A), (C) and (D) only

TrapFehling’s test is the one aromatic aldehydes fail; Tollens’ they pass.
Q964CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q37NTA final key

(D) Acetone(IV) Formic acid + Methanol

  2. (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
  3. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Concept to recallWith α-H: aldol (β-hydroxy carbonyl, dehydrating on heat to the enone/enal). Without α-H: Cannizzaro (acid salt + alcohol).
  1. (A) ethanal → aldol: 3-hydroxybutanal → but-2-enal (II).
  2. (B) methanal, no α-H → Cannizzaro: formate + methanol (IV).
  3. (C) benzaldehyde → Cannizzaro: benzoate + benzyl alcohol (I).
  4. (D) acetone → aldol: 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one → 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (III).

Q965CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q38NTA final key

  4. (B), (C) and (D) only

  2. (B) CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3: has CH3CH(OH)– — yes.
  3. (C) C6H5CH2CHO: no CH3CO– — no.
  4. (D) CH3COCH2CH2CH3: methyl ketone — yes.
  5. Answer: (A), (B) and (D) only.

Q966CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q39NTA final key
The correct order of increasing pKa values of the compounds :

  2. (B) CH3OCH2COOH

  2. (A) < (C) < (B) < (D)
  3. (B) < (A) < (C) < (D)
  4. (C) < (B) < (A) < (D)
Concept to recallIncreasing pKa = decreasing acid strength. −I groups (Cl, OCH3) strengthen the acid; +I groups (alkyl) weaken it.
  1. Cl3C–COOH (three −I Cl): strongest, pKa 0.7.
  2. CH3OCH2COOH (−I of O): pKa 3.5. CH3COOH: 4.76.
  3. (CH3)3CCOOH (+I of three CH3): weakest, 5.0.
  4. Increasing pKa: (C) < (B) < (A) < (D).

Q967CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q17 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. Formic acid
  3. Oxalic acid

Q968CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q2 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their boiling points
A. Ethoxyethane
B. n-Butane
C. Pentanal
D. Pentan-1-ol
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B > A > C > D
  2. D > C > A > B
  3. C > D > A > B
  4. A > B > D > C
Concept to recallSimilar molar mass: alcohols (H-bonding) > aldehydes (strong C=O dipole) > ethers (weak dipole) > alkanes (only dispersion).
  1. Pentan-1-ol: intermolecular H-bonds ⇒ highest (411 K).
  2. Pentanal: dipole–dipole from C=O (376 K).
  3. Ethoxyethane: weak dipole (308 K); n-butane: only van der Waals (273 K).
  4. D > C > A > B.

Answer: option (2) — D > C > A > B

Q969CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q21 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Choose the correct statement/statements for Cannizzaro reaction.

B. Takes place in aldehydes having absence of α-hydrogen
C. It is a disproportionation reaction
D. Get a mixture of carboxylic acid, salt and ethers
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C only
  2. B, C, D only
  3. B, C only
  4. A, C only
Concept to recallCannizzaro: an aldehyde with no α-H, with conc. alkali, is half oxidised (carboxylate salt) and half reduced (alcohol).
  1. A is wrong: ketones do not give Cannizzaro.
  2. B is right; C is right (self oxidation–reduction).
  3. D is wrong: the products are an alcohol and a carboxylate salt, no ether.

Answer: option (3) — B, C only

Q970CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q28 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Arrange the following in decreasing order of their reactivity towards nucleophilic addition reaction
A. CH3CHO
B. CH3CH2CHO
C. CH3COCH3
D. CH3COCH2CH3
E. C6H5COCH3
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C, D, E
  2. E, D, C, B, A
  3. E, D, C, A, B
  4. B, C, A, D, E
Concept to recallNucleophilic addition falls as alkyl groups add (+I lowers the C=O carbon’s positive charge, and bulk hinders attack); aryl conjugation lowers it further.
  1. Aldehydes before ketones: A, B before C, D.
  2. Bigger alkyl = slower: A > B, C > D.
  3. Acetophenone (resonance with ring) is least: A > B > C > D > E.

Answer: option (1) — A, B, C, D, E

Q971CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q7 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  1. 3,7,7-Trimethylhepta-2,6-dienal
  2. 2,6-Dimethylocta-2,6-dienal
  3. 3,7-Dimethylocta-2,6-dienal
  4. 2,6-Dimethylhepta-1,5-dien-1-al
Concept to recallThe CHO carbon is C-1 and is part of the chain; choose the longest chain containing it and both C=C, number from CHO.
  1. Chain from CHO: C1 (CHO), C2=C3(CH3), C4, C5, C6=C7(CH3), and one CH3 of C7 is C8.
  2. Eight carbons ⇒ octa; C=C at 2 and 6 ⇒ octa-2,6-dienal; methyls on 3 and 7.
  3. 3,7-Dimethylocta-2,6-dienal (citral).

Answer: option (3) — 3,7-Dimethylocta-2,6-dienal

NotePrepp’s skeletal drawing shows only one CH2 between the two C=C units (which would make a heptadienal matching no option); the options leave no doubt that citral, with two CH2 groups, is intended, and it is written so here.
Q972CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q13NTA final key

  4. Fehling’s test
Concept to recallFehling’s solution is reduced by aliphatic aldehydes but not by aromatic aldehydes.
  1. Both aldehydes give 2,4-DNP derivatives and silver mirrors.
  2. Only acetaldehyde gives the red Cu2O precipitate with Fehling’s.
  3. Neither reacts with NaHCO3 (that is a test for acids).

  2. Acetone has CH3CO– ⇒ iodoform positive.

  2. Ozonolysis of a disubstituted alkene carbon gives a ketone; RCN + R′MgX then hydrolysis gives RCOR′.
  3. Stephen reaction gives aldehydes only.

Q975CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q8NTA final key

  2. The free acid appears only after acidification.

Q977CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q14NTA final key

Q998CUET 2023 · 5 June, Shift 1 · Q41 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q1003CUET 2023 · 07 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q41key re-derived
Passage (summarised): carbonyl compounds

Compounds with a carbon–oxygen double bond (>C=O) are carbonyl compounds. The group is highly polar, so their boiling points are higher than those of hydrocarbons and ethers of similar mass. Aldehydes are made by dehydrogenation or oxidation of alcohols and by reduction of acyl halides; ketones by oxidation of secondary alcohols or hydration of alkynes. Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN, NaHSO3 and ammonia derivatives. Carboxylic acids are made by oxidising primary alcohols, aldehydes and alkenes, and by hydrolysing nitriles; they are more acidic than alcohols and phenols.

The product (A) is: 3-formylbenzoic acid (m-OHC–C6H4–COOH) ⟶ NaCN/HCl → A
  1. m-HOOC–C6H4–COOH
  2. m-HOOC–C6H4–CH(OH)CN
  3. m-HOOC–C6H4–CH2OH
  4. m-OHC–C6H4–CH(OH)CN
Concept to recallHCN (from NaCN/HCl) adds across C=O of an aldehyde to give a cyanohydrin, >C(OH)CN; a –COOH group does not react.
  1. Only the –CHO undergoes nucleophilic addition.
  2. –CHO → –CH(OH)CN; –COOH unchanged.

Answer: option (2) — m-HOOC–C6H4–CH(OH)CN

The correct increasing order of acidic strength is:

  2. C6H5CH2COOH < C6H5COOH < NO2CH2COOH < FCH2COOH
  3. C6H5CH2COOH < C6H5COOH < FCH2COOH < NO2CH2COOH
  4. C6H5COOH < FCH2COOH < C6H5CH2COOH < NO2CH2COOH

Q1005CUET 2023 · 07 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q43key re-derived
Passage (summarised): carbonyl compounds

Compounds with a carbon–oxygen double bond (>C=O) are carbonyl compounds. The group is highly polar, so their boiling points are higher than those of hydrocarbons and ethers of similar mass. Aldehydes are made by dehydrogenation or oxidation of alcohols and by reduction of acyl halides; ketones by oxidation of secondary alcohols or hydration of alkynes. Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN, NaHSO3 and ammonia derivatives. Carboxylic acids are made by oxidising primary alcohols, aldehydes and alkenes, and by hydrolysing nitriles; they are more acidic than alcohols and phenols.

The correct sequence of reagents for the conversion of 3-nitrobromobenzene to 3-nitrobenzoic acid is:
  1. Mg/ether, CO2, H3O+
  2. KCN, LiAlH4, NaOH
  3. KMnO4/OH−, dil. H2SO4, CO2/H+
  4. AgNO3 (ammoniacal), CO2, H3O+
Concept to recallArBr → ArMgBr (Mg, dry ether); ArMgBr + CO2 → ArCOOMgBr → (H3O+) ArCOOH.
  1. The Br carbon must become COOH: carboxylation of a Grignard reagent does exactly that.
  2. KCN does not displace an aryl Br, and LiAlH4 would reduce a nitrile to an amine; KMnO4 and Tollens’ do not act on C–Br.

Answer: option (1) — Mg/ether, CO2, H3O+

NoteThe reconstruction prints “H3O3”; read H3O+. Strictly a nitro group is attacked by Grignard reagents, so this route is the textbook answer rather than a practical one; it is the only option that turns C–Br into C–COOH.

Q1011CUET 2023 · 08 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q45worked here
Passage (summarised): formaldehyde

Formaldehyde, the first aldehyde, occurs in green leaves, where it is thought to form from CO2 and water in sunlight with chlorophyll. Commercially it is made by controlled oxidation of methane over a molybdenum oxide catalyst. It is a constituent of several polymers, the resins — non-volatile solids or semi-solids obtained from some plants and also made in the laboratory.

Benzaldehyde is less reactive towards nucleophilic addition reaction than formaldehyde because of:
  1. +R effect of >C=O group and steric factor due to phenyl group
  2. −I effect of >C=O group and steric factor due to phenyl group
  3. +I effect of >C=O group and steric factor due to phenyl group
  4. +I effect of >C=O group and steric factor due to phenyl group (printed twice)
Concept to recallIn benzaldehyde the ring donates electrons to C=O by resonance (+R), lowering its electrophilicity; the phenyl group also hinders the nucleophile.
  1. Resonance with the ring reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon (+R).
  2. Phenyl is bulkier than H (steric factor). Hence option (1).

Answer: option (1) — +R effect of >C=O group and steric factor due to phenyl group

NotePrepp’s unofficial key prints option (2). A −I effect would make the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic. Options (3) and (4) are printed identically in the reconstruction, and all four wrongly attribute the effect to the C=O group; the intended reason is the +R (resonance) electron release of the phenyl ring plus its bulk.
Q1012CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q30key re-derived
Which of the following compounds gives iodoform test?
  1. CH3OH
  2. CH3CH2OH
  3. C2H5COC2H5
  4. HCHO
Concept to recallIodoform test is positive for CH3CO– compounds and for CH3CH(OH)– alcohols (oxidised by I2/NaOH to CH3CO–).
  1. Ethanol → (I2/NaOH) CH3CHO → CHI3.
  2. Methanol, pentan-3-one and HCHO have no CH3CO– / CH3CH(OH)– unit.

Answer: option (2) — CH3CH2OH

Q1013CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q46key re-derived
Passage (summarised): aldehydes versus ketones

Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition, for steric and electronic reasons. Sterically, the two relatively large groups on a ketone hinder the approach of the nucleophile to the carbonyl carbon more than the single group of an aldehyde. Electronically, two alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more than one does.

If toluene ⟶ KMnO4/KOH, heat; H3O+ → benzoic acid, then C6H5CH2CH2CH3 ⟶ KMnO4/KOH, Δ; H3O+ → A. A will be:
  1. C6H5CH2CH2COOH
  2. C6H5CH2COOH
  3. C6H5COOH
  4. C6H5CH2CH(OH)CH3
Concept to recallVigorous KMnO4 oxidises any alkyl side chain with a benzylic H down to –COOH on the ring, whatever its length.
  1. The whole propyl chain is cut back to the benzylic carbon: A = benzoic acid.

Answer: option (3) — C6H5COOH

For preparation of phenylethanoic acid from benzyl alcohol, reagents required are
  1. (A) HBr
  2. (B) CO2
  3. (C) KCN
  4. (D) Δ/H3O+
  5. (E) AgNO3
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B and C only
  2. A, C and D only
  3. A, C and E only
  4. A, B and E only
Concept to recallAdding one carbon: R–OH → R–Br → R–CN → (hydrolysis) R–COOH.
  1. C6H5CH2OH + HBr → C6H5CH2Br; + KCN → C6H5CH2CN; H3O+/Δ → C6H5CH2COOH.
  2. Reagents A, C, D.

Answer: option (2) — A, C and D only

(B) Cyclohexene → hexanedioic acid (two COOH)(II) H3O+/Δ

(D) CH3CONH2 → CH3COOH(IV) KMnO4–H2SO4/Δ

  3. A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II (printed identically to option (2))

Q1017CUET 2023 · 10 Jun, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q50worked here
Passage (summarised): aldehydes versus ketones

In the reaction of carboxylic acids with ammonia to give the imides, the reaction proceeds in the sequence of steps involving the following compounds.
  1. (A) C6H4(CO)2NH (cyclic imide)
  2. (B) C6H4(COOH)2 (ortho)
  3. (C) C6H4(CONH2)2 (ortho)
  4. (D) C6H4(COO−NH4+)2 (ortho)
The correct sequence of the compounds formed will be:
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B, D, C, A
  2. B, C, D, A
  3. B, A, D, C
  4. B, C, A, D
Concept to recallRCOOH + NH3 → RCOO−NH4+ → (Δ, −H2O) RCONH2; a 1,2-diamide on strong heating loses NH3 to the cyclic imide.
  1. Phthalic acid (B) + NH3 → ammonium phthalate (D).
  2. Heat, −2H2O → phthalamide (C).
  3. Strong heating, −NH3 → phthalimide (A). Sequence B, D, C, A.

Answer: option (1) — B, D, C, A

NotePrepp’s unofficial key prints option (2). (B, C, D, A), which puts the amide before the ammonium salt; the acid first forms the salt with NH3 and only heating turns that into the amide (NCERT).
Q1018CUET 2023 · 11 Jun, Shift 3 · Q46 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Passage (summarised): nucleophilic addition to C=O

Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition. The nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon from a direction roughly perpendicular to the plane of its sp2 orbitals; the carbon becomes sp3 and a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate forms, which picks up H+ to give the neutral product. In carboxylic acids the carbonyl carbon is less electrophilic than in aldehydes and ketones.

The correct order of reactivity for addition reaction of following carbonyl compounds with C2H5MgI:
(I) HCHO   (II) (CH3)2C=O   (III) CH3CHO   (IV) ((CH3)3C)2C=O
(A) (I) > (III) > (II) > (IV)
(B) (IV) > (III) > (II) > (I)
(C) (I) > (II) > (IV) > (III)
(D) (III) > (II) > (I) > (IV)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (C)
  2. (D)
  3. (A)
  4. (B)
Concept to recallNucleophilic addition: fewer/smaller alkyl groups on C=O ⇒ less +I and less crowding ⇒ faster.
  1. HCHO (no alkyl) > CH3CHO (one) > acetone (two) > di-tert-butyl ketone (two bulky groups).
  2. I > III > II > IV, which is statement (A).

Answer: option (3) — (A)

  3. treating with sodium bisulphite and then hydrolysing
  4. treating with CH3MgBr followed by hydrolysis

  2. Hydrolysis of –CN to –COOH gives CH3CH(OH)COOH, lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid).

The optimum pH for carrying out the reaction of aldehyde with hydroxylamine to form oxime is:
  1. pH = 1
  2. pH = 4–5
  3. pH = 12
  4. Any pH
Concept to recallAmmonia-derivative condensations need a weakly acidic medium.
  1. Some acid protonates the C=O oxygen and makes the carbon more electrophilic.
  2. Too much acid protonates NH2OH itself, destroying the nucleophile; so the optimum is mildly acidic, pH ~4–5.

Answer: option (2) — pH = 4–5

Q1021CUET 2023 · 11 Jun, Shift 3 · Q49 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Passage (summarised): nucleophilic addition to C=O

Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition. An organic compound C3H6O does not give a precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine and also does not react with metallic sodium. It could be
  1. CH3CH2CHO
  2. CH2=CH–CH2OH
  3. CH3COCH3
  4. CH2=CH–O–CH3
Concept to recall2,4-DNP tests C=O; Na tests O–H.
  1. No 2,4-DNP precipitate: not an aldehyde or ketone — rules out propanal and acetone.
  2. No reaction with Na: no OH — rules out allyl alcohol.
  3. Left: methyl vinyl ether, CH2=CH–O–CH3.

Answer: option (4) — CH2=CH–O–CH3

Q1022CUET 2023 · 11 Jun, Shift 3 · Q50 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Choose the correct answer from the options given below (reaction : name):
(A) C6H5CH3 →(CrO2Cl2; H3O+) C6H5CHO (Etard reaction)
(B) RCOCl →(H2/Pd–BaSO4) RCHO + HCl (Rosenmund reduction)
(C) >C=O →(Zn–Hg, HCl) >CH2 + H2O (Clemmensen reduction)
(D) >C=O →(H2N–NH2; H3O+) >CH2 + H2O (Balz Schiemann reaction)
(E) C6H6 →(CO, HCl) C6H5CHO (Gattermann Koch reaction)
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D) only
  2. (B), (C), (D), (E) only
  3. (E), (A), (D) only
  4. (A), (B), (C), (E) only
Concept to recallC=O → CH2 with hydrazine then KOH/ethylene glycol is Wolff–Kishner; Balz–Schiemann makes ArF from ArN2+BF4−.
  1. A Etard, B Rosenmund, C Clemmensen, E Gattermann–Koch are all correctly named.
  2. D is a Wolff–Kishner reduction (and needs KOH/glycol, not acid), so its label is wrong.
  3. Correct set: A, B, C, E.

Answer: option (4) — (A), (B), (C), (E) only

NoteIn the reconstruction reaction (C) reads “Na, Hg / HCl”; the Clemmensen reagent is Zn–Hg/HCl, and the intended pairing (Clemmensen) is unambiguous.
Q1023CUET 2023 · 13 Jun, Shift 3 · Q12 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
What will be the product formed when cyclohexanone undergoes aldol condensation?
  1. cyclohexanol
  2. cyclohex-2-en-1-one
  3. 4-cyclohexylcyclohexan-1-one
  4. 2-cyclohexylidenecyclohexan-1-one
Concept to recallAldol condensation: the enolate of one carbonyl adds to the C=O of another; the β-hydroxy ketone then loses water to give an α,β-unsaturated ketone.
  1. The α-carbon of one cyclohexanone attacks the carbonyl carbon of the second.
  2. Dehydration puts a C=C between the α-carbon and the former carbonyl carbon: two rings joined by a C=C, one still carrying C=O next to the junction.

Answer: option (4) — 2-cyclohexylidenecyclohexan-1-one

Q1032CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q48NTA final key
Passage: Certain aldehydes, ketones and certain alcohols undergo the iodoform test. Certain aldehydes and ketones undergo aldol condensation, while certain aldehydes undergo Cannizzaro’s reaction. Aldehydes respond to Tollens’ reagent and Fehling’s reagent test.
When CH3CHO and HCHO are treated with NaOH (aq), one of the product is found to be C(CH2OH)4 [HOCH2–C(CH2OH)2–CH2OH]. The number of times aldol condensation and number of times Cannizzaro’s reaction occur to produce the product is
  1. 1, 3
  2. 3, 1
  3. 2, 2
  4. 1, 1
Concept to recallPentaerythritol: three crossed aldols (one per α-H of CH3CHO) then one crossed Cannizzaro with HCHO.
  1. Each of the three α-H of CH3CHO adds to one HCHO → (HOCH2)3C–CHO (3 aldols).
  2. This aldehyde has no α-H; HCHO reduces it to C(CH2OH)4 (1 Cannizzaro).

Answer: option (2) — 3, 1

Q1033CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q49NTA final key
Passage: Certain aldehydes, ketones and certain alcohols undergo the iodoform test. Certain aldehydes and ketones undergo aldol condensation, while certain aldehydes undergo Cannizzaro’s reaction. Aldehydes respond to Tollens’ reagent and Fehling’s reagent test.
Which amongst the following will respond to Tollen’s reagent test.
  1. A. C6H5CHO (benzaldehyde)
  2. B. HCHO
  3. C. HCOOH
  4. D. CH3COCH3
Choose the correct option
  1. A and B only
  2. A, B and C only
  3. B and C only
  4. D only
Concept to recallTollens’ reagent is reduced by all aldehydes (aliphatic and aromatic) and by formic acid (it has an H–C=O unit).
  1. Benzaldehyde and HCHO are aldehydes → silver mirror.
  2. HCOOH also reduces Tollens’ reagent.
  3. Acetone does not → A, B and C.

Answer: option (2) — A, B and C only

TrapFehling’s solution is NOT reduced by aromatic aldehydes; Tollens’ is.
Q1034CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q50NTA final key
Passage: Certain aldehydes, ketones and certain alcohols undergo the iodoform test. Certain aldehydes and ketones undergo aldol condensation, while certain aldehydes undergo Cannizzaro’s reaction. Aldehydes respond to Tollens’ reagent and Fehling’s reagent test.

  1. C6H5CHO (benzaldehyde)
  2. CH3CHO
  3. CH3COCH3
  4. C6H5COCH3 (acetophenone)
Concept to recallFehling’s test: aliphatic aldehydes only; Tollens’: all aldehydes.
  1. Ketones give neither test; benzaldehyde gives Tollens’ but not Fehling’s.
  2. Acetaldehyde gives both.

Q1035CUET 2023 · 22 Jun, Shift 2 · Q2NTA final key

  2. CH3–CH2–CH=C(CH3)–CH3 → (i) O3, (ii) Zn/H2O

  4. CH3CH2COCl → H2/Pd
Concept to recallAldehyde routes: DIBAL-H on esters, ozonolysis of alkenes, Rosenmund reduction of acid chlorides; strong oxidants (KMnO4) take a 1° alcohol right through to the acid.

Q1036CUET 2023 · 22 Jun, Shift 2 · Q30NTA final key
Predict the products in the given reaction: m-chlorobenzaldehyde (3-ClC6H4CHO) → 50% KOH
  1. 3-ClC6H4CH2OH + 3-ClC6H4CH2COO−
  2. 3-HOC6H4CH2OH + C6H4(OH)2 (resorcinol)
  3. 3-ClC6H4CH2OH + 3-ClC6H4COO−
  4. 3-HOC6H4CH2OH + C6H5COO−
Concept to recallCannizzaro: an aldehyde without α-H in conc. alkali disproportionates into the alcohol and the carboxylate.
  1. Aryl C–Cl is untouched by aqueous KOH.
  2. 2 ArCHO + OH− → ArCH2OH + ArCOO− (Ar = 3-chlorophenyl).

Answer: option (3) — 3-ClC6H4CH2OH + 3-ClC6H4COO−

NoteStructures in the paper are written here as condensed formulas.
Q1037CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q12NTA final key
Aldehydes form gem-dialkoxy compound when they are reacted with:
  1. one equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride
  2. two equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride
  3. ethylene glycol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride
  4. hydrogen cyanide in the presence of sodium hydroxide
Concept to recallRCHO + R′OH (dry HCl) → hemiacetal; + a second R′OH → acetal RCH(OR′)2, a gem-dialkoxy alkane.
  1. One equivalent stops at the hemiacetal (one OR, one OH).
  2. Two equivalents give the acetal: two alkoxy groups on the same carbon (gem-dialkoxy).
  3. Ethylene glycol gives a cyclic acetal (a ring, 1,3-dioxolane) and HCN gives a cyanohydrin.

Answer: option (2) — two equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride

TrapEthylene glycol does give an acetal, but a cyclic ketal/acetal, not two separate alkoxy groups.
Q1038CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q16NTA final key
Addition of HCN to carbonyl group results in formation of:
  1. Cyanides
  2. Isocyanide
  3. Cyano hydrins
  4. Aldehyeles
Concept to recallNucleophilic addition: CN− attacks the carbonyl carbon; protonation of O gives R2C(OH)CN, a cyanohydrin.
  1. >C=O + HCN (base catalyst) → >C(OH)CN.
  2. The product carries both −OH and −CN on one carbon: a cyanohydrin.

Answer: option (3) — Cyano hydrins

Q1039CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q28NTA final key
Match List – I with List – II.
List – IList – II
(A) Clemensen reduction(I) C6H5CH3 –(CrO2Cl2; H3O+)→ C6H5CHO
(B) Kolbe’s reaction(II) >C=O –(NH2NH2; H3O+)→ >CH2
(C) Etard reaction(III) >C=O + HCl –(NaHg)→ >CH2
(D) Wolf Kishner reduction(IV) C6H5OH –(CO2; NaOH, H+)→ o-HOC6H4COOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  2. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  3. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Concept to recallClemmensen: Zn-Hg/conc. HCl, C=O → CH2. Wolff–Kishner: NH2NH2 then KOH/glycol, C=O → CH2. Étard: CrO2Cl2 oxidises Ar–CH3 to Ar–CHO. Kolbe: sodium phenoxide + CO2 → salicylic acid.
  1. Clemmensen (amalgam + HCl) → III.
  2. Kolbe (phenol + CO2/NaOH) → IV.
  3. Étard (chromyl chloride on toluene) → I.
  4. Wolff–Kishner (hydrazine) → II.

Answer: option (4) — (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

Q1040CUET 2023 · 23 Jun, Shift 3 · Q32NTA final key
CH3–CO–CH2–CO–OC2H5 –A– CH3–C(OH)=CH–CO–OC2H5
CH3–CO–O–H –B– CH3–C(O−)=O+–H
A and B represent:
  1. Tautomerism and Resonance
  2. Metamerism and Resonance
  3. Resonance and Tautomerism
  4. Metamerism and Tautomerism
Concept to recallTautomers are real isomers in equilibrium that differ in the position of an H atom (keto ⇌ enol). Resonance structures differ only in the placement of electrons; the atoms stay put.
  1. A: an H moves from CH2 to O and a C=C appears → keto–enol tautomerism (ethyl acetoacetate).
  2. B: no atom moves; a lone pair on OH and the π electrons of C=O shift → resonance.

Answer: option (1) — Tautomerism and Resonance

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Tautomerism and resonance are Class XI organic chemistry. Both arrows are double-headed in the paper.
Q1041CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q11NTA final key
When 1,3-Diphenylprop-2-en-1-one is formed by the reaction of benzaldehyde and acetophenone in the presence of dil. NaOH followed by heating, which is the correct option?
  1. Acetophenone acts as Electrophile
  2. Benzaldehyde acts as Nucleophile
  3. Acetophenone acts as Nucleophile
  4. Benzaldehyde has an α-hydrogen
Concept to recallCross (Claisen–Schmidt) aldol: the carbonyl compound with α-H forms the enolate (nucleophile); the one without α-H (benzaldehyde) is the electrophile.
  1. Benzaldehyde has no α-H, so it cannot form an enolate.
  2. OH− removes an α-H of acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) → enolate, the nucleophile.
  3. It attacks the C=O of benzaldehyde; dehydration on heating gives chalcone, C6H5CO–CH=CH–C6H5.

Answer: option (3) — Acetophenone acts as Nucleophile

Q1042CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q12NTA final key
Aldol condensation results due to:
  1. Acidity of α-hydrogen in aldehydes and ketones
  2. Acidity of α-hydrogen in carboxylic acids
  3. Acidity of α-hydrogen in amines
  4. Acidity of α-hydrogen in Haloalkanes
Concept to recallα-H of aldehydes/ketones is acidic because the carbanion (enolate) is stabilised by resonance with C=O.
  1. Base removes an α-H of an aldehyde or ketone to give a resonance-stabilised enolate.
  2. The enolate adds to another carbonyl group: aldol.

Answer: option (1) — Acidity of α-hydrogen in aldehydes and ketones

Q1043CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q24NTA final key
2,4-DNP is ______
  1. 2,4-Dinitrophenol
  2. 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine
  3. 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazone
  4. 2,4-Dinitrophenylacetic acid
Concept to recallBrady’s reagent, 2,4-DNP = 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine; with aldehydes and ketones it gives yellow-orange 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazones.
  1. In the carbonyl tests, 2,4-DNP is the reagent 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine.
  2. The hydrazone is the product it forms, not the reagent.

Answer: option (2) — 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine

Trap“2,4-DNP” is also used for 2,4-dinitrophenol elsewhere, but in carbonyl chemistry it means the hydrazine.
Q1044CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q25NTA final key
Select the reagents a and b respectively, used in the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction:
R–CH2COOH –(a; b)→ R–CH(X)–COOH   (X = Cl, Br)
  1. (A) X2
  2. (B) X2 / Red Phosphorus
  3. (C) H2O
  4. (D) SOCl2
  5. (E) X2 / Yellow Phosphorus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A and C only
  2. B and C only
  3. D and E only
  4. C and D only
Concept to recallHVZ: RCH2COOH + X2/red P, then H2O → RCH(X)COOH (α-halogenation of acids with α-H).
  1. a = X2 with red phosphorus (forms PX3, then the acyl halide, which halogenates at α).
  2. b = water, to hydrolyse the α-halo acyl halide back to the acid. Answer: B and C.

Answer: option (2) — B and C only

Q1045CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q30NTA final key

(A) Rosenmund reduction(I) CrO2Cl2, CS2; H3O+

Q1046CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q39NTA final key
Arrange the following in increasing order of their boiling points:
  1. (A) CH3CH2CH2CHO
  2. (B) CH3CH2CH2CH2OH
  3. (C) C2H5OC2H5
  4. (D) CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3
  5. (E) CH3CH2CH2COOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. D < E < B < A < C
  2. D < E < A < B < C
  3. D < C < A < E < B
  4. D < C < A < B < E
Concept to recallFor comparable molar masses: hydrocarbon < ether < aldehyde/ketone (dipole) < alcohol (H-bond) < carboxylic acid (H-bonded dimers).
  1. Acid (butanoic, 437 K) > alcohol (butan-1-ol, 391 K) > aldehyde (butanal, 348 K) > ether and alkane.
  2. NCERT’s ordering puts the ether above the alkane: D < C < A < B < E.

Answer: option (4) — D < C < A < B < E

NoteMeasured values for these two are almost equal (pentane 309 K, ethoxyethane 308 K); the key follows the textbook trend that a polar ether boils above an alkane of similar mass.
Q1047CUET 2022 · 10 Aug, Shift 1 (SET 06) · Q31NTA final key

Concept to recallNaBH4 is a mild hydride donor: it reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols but leaves esters (and acids) untouched.
  1. The ring C=O (ketone) is reduced to CH–OH.
  2. The ester –COOCH3 is not attacked by NaBH4.
  3. Product: methyl 2-(2-hydroxycyclohexyl)ethanoate — structure (2).

Answer: option (2) —

TrapLiAlH4 would also reduce the ester (to a diol); NaBH4 does not.
Q1048CUET 2022 · 10 Aug, Shift 1 (SET 06) · Q34NTA final key

Q1049CUET 2022 · 10 Aug, Shift 1 (SET 06) · Q35NTA final key
Which simple chemical test is used to distinguish between ethanal & propanal?
  1. Iodoform test
  2. Tollen’s test
  3. Fehling’s test
  4. Lucas test
Concept to recallIodoform test is given by CH3CO– compounds (and CH3CH(OH)–); ethanal is the only aldehyde that gives it.
  1. Ethanal CH3CHO has CH3CO– ⇒ yellow CHI3.
  2. Propanal CH3CH2CHO does not.
  3. Both aldehydes respond to Tollens’ and Fehling’s; Lucas is a test for alcohols.

Answer: option (1) — Iodoform test

Q1050CUET 2022 · 10 Aug, Shift 1 (SET 06) · Q36NTA final key
Which of the following compound would undergo Aldol condensation?
  1. Methanal
  2. Benzaldehyde
  3. 2,2- Dimethylbutanal
  4. Phenylacetaldehyde
Concept to recallAldol condensation needs at least one α-hydrogen (dilute alkali forms an enolate).
  1. Methanal and benzaldehyde have no α-H.
  2. 2,2-dimethylbutanal: α-carbon is quaternary (no H).
  3. Phenylacetaldehyde C6H5CH2CHO has two α-H ⇒ aldol.

Answer: option (4) — Phenylacetaldehyde

TrapAldehydes without α-H give the Cannizzaro reaction instead.

Q1051CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q31NTA final key
The first step in conversion of aniline to 4-bromoaniline involves
  1. Acetylation of amino group
  2. Formation of diazonium salt in the presence of NaNO2 and HCl.
  3. Reaction with Bromine water at room temperature.
  4. Reaction with Bromine in the presence of NaOH.
Concept to recall–NH2 activates the ring so strongly that Br2 water gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Acetylation tones it down (lone pair shared with C=O) so mono-substitution at para is possible.
  1. Protect: aniline + (CH3CO)2O → acetanilide.
  2. Brominate: p-bromoacetanilide (major).
  3. Hydrolyse: 4-bromoaniline.

Answer: option (1) — Acetylation of amino group

TrapBromine water straight on aniline gives the 2,4,6-tribromo product, a white precipitate.
Q1052CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q32NTA final key
Which of the following reagents will bring out the following transformation?
(A) NaNO2/HCl and Cu/HCl
(B) NaNO2/NaOH and Cu/HCl
(C) NaNO2/HCl and Cu2Cl2/HCl
(D) NaNO2/NaOH and Cu2Cl2/HCl
  1. (A) and (C) only
  2. (A), (B) and (D) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallDiazotisation needs nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl, 273–278 K). ArN2+Cl− → ArCl with Cu2Cl2/HCl (Sandmeyer) or Cu powder/HCl (Gattermann).
  1. NaNO2/NaOH makes no HNO2, so (B) and (D) cannot diazotise.
  2. (A) Gattermann and (C) Sandmeyer both work.

Answer: option (1) — (A) and (C) only

Q1053CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q33NTA final key
Amongst the following, the strongest base in the aqueous medium is:
  1. CH3NH2
  2. NCCH2NH2
  3. (CH3)2NH
  4. C6H5NHCH3
Concept to recallIn water, for methyl amines: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N (inductive effect + solvation). –CN (−I) and phenyl (resonance) weaken basicity.
  1. NCCH2NH2: the cyano group withdraws electrons, weak base.
  2. C6H5NHCH3: lone pair delocalised into the ring, weak base.
  3. Dimethylamine (2°) beats methylamine in water: strongest.

Answer: option (3) — (CH3)2NH

Q1054CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q34NTA final key
Select the correct set of reagents required for conversion of the following chemical reactions
  1. (i). NaNO2/HCl, 273-278 K (ii). H3PO4, H2O (iii). KMnO4 and KOH
  2. (i). NaNO2/HCl (ii). H3PO4 (iii). NaOH/H2O
  3. (i). HNO3/H2SO4 (ii). H3PO4 (iii). KMnO4 and KOH
  4. (i). NaNO2/HCl (ii). Sn/HCl (iii). KMnO4 and KOH
Concept to recallDeamination: ArNH2 → ArN2+ → ArH with hypophosphorous acid (H3PO2). Alkaline KMnO4 oxidises a side-chain CH3 on a ring to COOH.
  1. The NH2 is gone and CH3 has become COOH; Br is unchanged.
  2. Diazotise at 273–278 K, replace N2+ by H, then oxidise CH3 with KMnO4/KOH.
  3. Only the first set has diazotisation, the reducing replacement and the oxidation in that order.

Answer: option (1) — (i). NaNO2/HCl, 273-278 K (ii). H3PO4, H2O (iii). KMnO4 and KOH

NoteThe paper prints H3PO4 in every option; the reagent that replaces N2+ by H is hypophosphorous acid, H3PO2. The intended answer is unaffected.
Q1055CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 1 · Q36NTA final key
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis of amines produces
  1. tertiary amines.
  2. secondary amines.
  3. primary amines.
  4. aromatic secondary amines.
Concept to recallPhthalimide →(KOH) potassium phthalimide →(R–X) N-alkylphthalimide →(NaOH aq) R–NH2.
  1. The N carries only one alkyl group and is freed as RNH2: pure primary aliphatic amines.
  2. Aryl halides do not react with the phthalimide anion, so aromatic primary amines cannot be made this way.

Answer: option (3) — primary amines.

Q1056CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q26NTA final key
What would be the product X in the following chemical reaction?
Aniline →(i) NaNO2 + HCl; ii) H2O, warm) A →(CHCl3 + aq. NaOH; H3O+) X
  1. Salicylic acid
  2. Benzoquinone
  3. Salicylaldehyde
  4. 4-Hydroxybenzoic acid
Concept to recallArN2+ + warm water → phenol. Phenol + CHCl3/NaOH (Reimer–Tiemann) → o-hydroxybenzaldehyde.
  1. Diazotise aniline; warming the diazonium salt in water gives phenol (A).
  2. Reimer–Tiemann formylates at ortho: X = salicylaldehyde.

Answer: option (3) — Salicylaldehyde

TrapCCl4 instead of CHCl3 would give salicylic acid.
Q1057CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q46NTA final key
Passage (summarised): Amines (6 June 2026, Q46–50)

Amines are basic organic compounds derived by replacing one or more H of ammonia by alkyl or aryl groups; they occur in proteins, vitamins, alkaloids and hormones (adrenaline and ephedrine, both secondary amines, raise blood pressure). The N is sp3 with a lone pair, so the molecule is pyramidal and the C–N–E angle (E = C or H) is less than 109.5°. Basic strength depends on inductive, solvation and steric effects. Amines are primary, secondary or tertiary by the number of H replaced; they are made by reducing nitro compounds, nitriles and amides; 1° and 2° amines are hydrogen bonded; aliphatic and aromatic 1° amines give the carbylamine reaction; benzenediazonium chloride, a colourless crystalline solid, is made from aniline with NaNO2 and HCl at 273–278 K.

Select the correct order of boiling points of isomeric amines
  1. n-C4H9NH2 > (C2H5)2NH > C2H5N(CH3)2
  2. n-C4H9NH2 < (C2H5)2NH < C2H5N(CH3)2
  3. n-C4H9NH2 = (C2H5)2NH > C2H5N(CH3)2
  4. n-C4H9NH2 > (C2H5)2NH = C2H5N(CH3)2
Concept to recallIsomeric amines: 1° (two N–H for H-bonding) > 2° (one N–H) > 3° (none).
  1. Butan-1-amine 350.8 K > diethylamine 329.3 K > ethyldimethylamine 310.5 K (NCERT).

Answer: option (1) — n-C4H9NH2 > (C2H5)2NH > C2H5N(CH3)2

  2. N,N-Dimethylaniline

  4. 2,4,6-tribromoaniline

Q1059CUET 2026 · 6 June, Shift 1 · Q48NTA final key
Passage (summarised): Amines (6 June 2026, Q46–50)

Amines are basic organic compounds derived by replacing one or more H of ammonia by alkyl or aryl groups; they occur in proteins, vitamins, alkaloids and hormones (adrenaline and ephedrine, both secondary amines, raise blood pressure). The N is sp3 with a lone pair, so the molecule is pyramidal and the C–N–E angle (E = C or H) is less than 109.5°. Basic strength depends on inductive, solvation and steric effects. Amines are primary, secondary or tertiary by the number of H replaced; they are made by reducing nitro compounds, nitriles and amides; 1° and 2° amines are hydrogen bonded; aliphatic and aromatic 1° amines give the carbylamine reaction; benzenediazonium chloride, a colourless crystalline solid, is made from aniline with NaNO2 and HCl at 273–278 K.

Identify the correct decreasing order of basic strength of amines in aqueous solution.
  1. (C2H5)3N, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2, NH3
  2. C2H5NH2, (C2H5)3N, (C2H5)2NH, NH3
  3. NH3, C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, (C2H5)3N
  4. (C2H5)2NH, (C2H5)3N, C2H5NH2, NH3
Concept to recallIn water: ethyl series 2° > 3° > 1° > NH3; methyl series 2° > 1° > 3° > NH3 (+I effect, solvation of the cation, steric hindrance).

  1. m-Bromobenzylamine (3-Br–C6H4–CH2NH2)
  2. m-Bromoaniline (3-Br–C6H4–NH2)
